web_evidence.note: A named reviewer explicitly describes Katabasis as using a close-third-person narrator, noting that only short contemplative chapters depart from that close perspective; those departures are not described as first- or second-person character narration.

search_log: Searched for "Katabasis R.F. Kuang" with excerpt, first chapter, point of view, third person, narrator, and HarperCollins terms.
Opened and inspected BookBrowse's four-page authorized Harper Voyager excerpt; the sustained opening is close-third narration centered on Alice.
Opened Google Books; its publisher metadata verified the edition and offered a broad preview index, but the catalog synopsis was not used as person evidence.
Opened a whole-book Tournament of Books review that explicitly identifies the close-third-person narrator and discusses the short contemplative interchapters.

Opened a review describing Alice as the main POV for most of the novel and Peter as receiving a few later POV chapters; because it did not explicitly name grammatical person, it was used only as corroborative context and not recorded as standalone evidence.

Ran exact-quote searches for the isolated first-person and generic-you Goodreads passages. Context recovered for generic-you passages placed them inside Alice-centered third-person narration, while the first-person snippets remained insufficiently attributed.
Indigo's advertised chapter-one excerpt returned a 404 when opened; unauthorized full-text and chapter-mirror results were not used as cited evidence.
person_note: The controlling narration is close third person, chiefly centered on Alice, with some later Peter focalization that remains compatible with THIRD. The Goodreads evidence repeatedly supplies sustained she/her close narration, and the authorized opening independently shows the same form. Generic you passages are aphoristic or free-indirect generalizations, not sustained second-person narration. Two isolated I passages lack quotation boundaries or attribution in the quote export; given the explicit whole-book close-third description and absence of evidence for sustained first-person sections, they are treated as locally unclear rather than as competing base narration. The short contemplative interchapters vary focal distance or voice but available structural evidence does not establish a change of grammatical person.
